title: Relative Entropy Decay via BKM coercivity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
abstract: We introduce the notion of the BKM coercivity constant and show that the positivity of this constant governs the exponential relative entropy decay of the semigroup. Indeed, we prove that the modified log-Sobolev constant is equivalent to the BKM coercivity constant up to a constant depending on the asymptotic conditional expectation. We also discover that the BKM coercivity constants for matrix amplifications are already attained with a qubit auxiliary system, which also coincides with the GNS spectral gap of the generating Lindbladian. As a corollary, we establish a criterion that the complete modified log-Sobolev inequality holds if and only if the GNS gap of the semigroup is strictly positive. All the discussion above applies to quantum Markov semigroups that admit a faithful asymptotic conditional expectation as long-time equilibration, with no detailed balance condition assumed. As an application, we show the finite-dimensional Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyén Gibbs samplers always satisfy the complete modified log-Sobolev inequality.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to characterize the rate of convergence (relative entropy decay) in open quantum systems governed by Quantum Markov Semigroups. It introduces the BKM coercivity constant, proving that its positivity is equivalent to the system satisfying the Modified Log-Sobolev Inequality. This provides a general criterion for thermalization that does not require the system to obey detailed balance.
main_problem: The paper aims to quantify the exponential decay rate of the relative entropy for Quantum Markov Semigroups (QMS) using the BKM coercivity constant.
main_result: It establishes that the Modified Log-Sobolev Inequality (MLSI) holds if and only if the BKM coercivity constant is strictly positive, providing a criterion independent of the detailed balance condition.
method: The authors relate the MLSI constant ($\alpha(L)$) to the BKM coercivity constant ($\lambda_{	ext{BKM}}(L)$) and the GNS spectral gap ($\lambda_{	ext{GNS}}(L)$) through rigorous mathematical inequalities.
model_or_system: The study concerns general Quantum Markov Semigroups, described by time-homogeneous open quantum systems evolving via a Lindbladian $L$. Applications include analyzing the decay properties of specific samplers like the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyén (CKG) Gibbs sampler.
key_observables: Relative Entropy ($D(ho\|\sigma)$), MLSI constant ($\alpha(L)$), BKM coercivity constant ($\lambda_{	ext{BKM}}(L)$), and the GNS spectral gap ($\lambda_{	ext{GNS}}(L)$).
important_parameters: The decay rate $\alpha(L)$ is compared to the structural constants $\lambda_{	ext{BKM}}(L)$ and $\lambda_{	ext{GNS}}(L)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a faithful asymptotic conditional expectation $E$ as the long-time equilibrium state, and the results are shown to hold without assuming detailed balance.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by introducing the BKM coercivity constant and relating it to the MLSI. It then proves key theorems linking these constants and extends the results to the case where no detailed balance is assumed. Finally, it applies these criteria to specific physical models, such as the CKG sampler.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, general mathematical tools (BKM coercivity) to characterize the rate of thermalization and convergence in open quantum systems, which is central to understanding quantum dynamics in statistical mechanics.
